title: The Price Begins to Manifest
next_chapter_hook: Just as consciousness was about to return to his body, Chen Ji saw Su Qingyao looking back in bewilderment among the crowd—in those eyes, there was not a trace of memory of him.

text.content: At the moment when fate diverged, Chen Ji felt as though he was being torn in two. One half remained at this moment, witnessing the dramatic changes in the Three Realms; the other half was involuntarily drawn by that nascent possibility, falling toward an unknown direction. The will of the Heavenly Eye receded like a tide, but what replaced it was an even heavier oppression—the Tianji Record itself was trembling. Mo Xiansheng's fragmented voice came from the first page, carrying an unprecedented gravity: "Child, you have succeeded. But Heaven never makes a loss-making deal... The price has already begun to be collected."

Chen Ji turned sharply. His perception extended like a tide toward the mortal realm, passing through layers of void, attempting to lock onto that familiar trajectory of fate. However, in that instant, his heart felt as if gripped tightly by an invisible hand—Su Qingyao's thread of fate, the bond he had secretly guarded for countless years and poured countless心血 into, was becoming blurred and thin at a visible speed, as if something was erasing it piece by piece. "No..." Chen Ji's voice was hoarse and nearly out of tune. He wanted to grasp something, but found his fingers could only pass through emptiness.

dialogue.content: (Mo Xiansheng's voice came hauntingly from the fragmented page, carrying the vicissitudes of ten thousand years) "The price of the Tianji Record has always been an equivalent exchange. You saw futures others could not see, you rewrote fates that were destined to happen—therefore, your most cherished things must be used to fill this gap." After a pause, there was even a trace of compassion in his voice, "Su Qingyao... her bond with you is the anchor point of all your plans. Now, Heaven wants this anchor back."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. He saw—at the mountain gate of the Tianqing Sect in the mortal realm, Su Qingyao was standing there in a daze, holding a Jade Pendant that Chen Ji had once given her with his own hands. That was the token she had pretended to嫌弃 during their first mission together but had kept treasured to this day. But at this moment, there was not a trace of emotion in her eyes, as if it were just an ordinary stone. She even frowned slightly, seemingly puzzled why she was holding such a thing. "Chen Ji..." She pronounced this name, her tone flat as if reciting a stranger's name, "Who?"

dialogue.content: (Su Qingyao stood at the mountain gate, sunlight casting a long shadow behind her. Her fingertips rubbed against the patterns on the Jade Pendant, her brow creasing tighter and tighter) "Strange... Where did this thing come from? Why do I have this..." She couldn't remember. No matter how hard she tried, she couldn't. That figure who had fought alongside her on countless late nights, thattrash junior brother who always spoke the most shocking words in the mostcalm tone—in her memory, there was only blinding blankness. She tossed the Jade Pendant casually into a nearby stream, turned and left, her steps light, as if unloading some invisible burden.

text.content: Chen Ji watched that Jade Pendant tumble and sink in the stream water, finally disappearing from sight. His fingers cramped like a claw, knuckles white, but he made no sound. Did it hurt? Of course it hurt. That was a Jade Pendant he personally selected; to find it, he had waited three days and three nights atop a snowy mountain, just for that morning light to illuminate the jade vein. But at this moment, he didn't even have the right to pain—because all of this was his own choice. "Keep watching." He heard his own voice, calm to the point of being cold, "Who else..."

The answer came faster and more brutally than he imagined. When his perception turned toward the direction of the Demonic Holy Sect, he saw Ye Qing. This ally who had made a blood oath with him and shared the gear of fate was standing atop the Holy Sect's high tower, surrounded by familiar demonic mist. But within that mist, Chen Ji saw a crack—the crystallization of the contract between him and Ye Qing, now崩解 piece by piece. Ye Qing also seemed to sense something; she turned sharply, looking toward where Chen Ji was, lips moving but unable to utter any sound. "Chen Ji... where are you..." Her eyes reddened, her voice carrying unprecedented panic, "Why... I can't remember you..."

Two threads of fate, three bonds of connection, were dissipating at the same speed. Chen Ji felt his carefully laid plans being dismantled piece by piece by an invisible hand; those networks of relationships he had woven with countless心血 were becoming a tangled mess. Ye Qing, Su Qingyao... who else? He dared not continue looking, because he knew that according to the rules of the Tianji Record, the price always started from收取 his most precious things. And his most precious things had never been just these two women—there were also the pieces he had placed throughout the world, those allies who were alive today because of him, those innocent people who had been spared becoming sacrifices of fate because of him. "Enough." Mo Xiansheng's voice interrupted him, "You now have three choices."

choice.prompt: The rules of the Tianji Record were clear and ruthless: the third path to break the chains of fate required the most precious bonds to pave the way. Chen Ji stood at the crossroads of fate, facing bonds about to dissipate, he had to make a choice—

choices.text: Bear the price, sever the bonds
choices.description: Accept Heaven's rules, letting Su Qingyao and Ye Qing lose all memories of you, in exchange for the continued extension of the third path. This is the fastest and most direct method, but the price is you will be truly alone.
choices.visible_cost: Lose all core bonds, Su Qingyao and Ye Qing will never remember you
choices.visible_reward: The third path will be completely stabilized, Heaven's Eye's monitoring will further weaken
choices.risk_hint: You will become a true loner, all plans need to start over

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes. His fingers traced an arc in the air—that was the thread of bond between him, Su Qingyao, and Ye Qing. At this moment, they trembled at his fingertips, like two flames about to extinguish. "I'm sorry." He said softly, his voice without a trace of tremor, "This path... I must continue." He suddenly tightened his fingers. The flames extinguished. The two threads of fate became emptiness at the same instant, disappearing completely from this world—not forgotten, but never having existed.

choices.text: Reverse the price, retain the senior sister
choices.description: Channel the fate power sealed within the Tianji Record Fragment back, forcibly stabilizing the bonds between Su Qingyao and Ye Qing. But this approach will cause the third path to regress, and you will bear double the fate backlash.
choices.visible_cost: The third path regresses, Heavenly Fate consumption doubles, and will trigger further attention from Heaven
choices.visible_reward: Su Qingyao and Ye Qing retain their memories, your bonds will continue in a more stabilized form
choices.risk_hint: Heaven's gaze will become more obvious, future breakthroughs will become more difficult

text.content: Chen Ji forcefully activated the Tianji Record. The runes on the fragmented page flashed madly, a majestic power gushing forth, sweeping toward the mortal realm and the direction of the Demonic Holy Sect. He could feel his Heavenly Fate Value rapidly depleting, as if an invisible giant hand was extracting the essence of life from within him. "Come back..." He gritted his teeth, veins on his forehead standing out, "Come back to me!" Those two threads of fate about to dissipate, under his不惜代价 efforts, finally solidified again. But at the same time, a cold gaze descended from the depths of the celestial vault—the Heavenly Eye, it had seen everything.

choices.description: Not completely sever, nor forcibly retain, but divide the bonds—Su Qingyao retains partial memories, Ye Qing's contract continues in a fragmented form. This is a dangerous middle path, which may lead to unexpected consequences.
choices.visible_cost: The bond exists in an incomplete form, which may generate unpredictable variables in the future.
choices.visible_reward: Retaining partial strategic capability, the third path continues in an imperfect yet acceptable manner.
choices.risk_hint: Incomplete bonds may become vulnerabilities that future enemies can exploit.

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and made the choice he was best at—incomplete victory. He guided the power of the Tianji Record toward those two threads of destiny, neither severing nor strengthening them, but cutting. He voluntarily gave up a portion of the bonds' completeness, allowing them to persist in a fragmented form. In Su Qingyao's mind, there would remain a vague shadow, a figure she could never remember who it was, yet would inexplicably trust; Ye Qing's contract still existed, but every so often, she would experience a violent headache, as if something important was draining from her memories.

In that moment of decision, Chen Ji sensed something being torn from within him. Not his Heavenly Fate value, not his power, but something far more precious—the final tenderness connecting him to this world. He stood in the void, watching Su Qingyao turn and leave at the mountain gate, watching Ye Qing search in bewilderment atop the tower, watching those bonds he once believed he could forever protect transform into unfamiliar mist in their eyes. From now on, he would walk back into their lives as a complete stranger. This path was destined to be lonelier and more perilous.

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul materialized from the first page, his features more withered than ever before, as if having just endured some tremendous depletion. "You've chosen the most treacherous path." His voice carried no reproach, only a sigh of profound understanding. "Incomplete bonds... they will torment your heart like dull blades. Yet precisely this incompleteness allows the Heavenly Eye to momentarily lower its guard." His gaze settled upon Chen Ji with intricate emotion. "Your strategies must fundamentally shift from this moment. Remember, from now on, every person beside you could become either your chess piece or your fatal vulnerability."

text.content: Chen Ji nodded, yet did not immediately respond. His attention was entirely focused on the mortal realm—Su Qingyao had returned to the Tianqing Sect's Inner Sect, resuming her daily routines. Her expression remained coldly composed, her movements crisp and efficient, as if that night of secretly examining the trinkets Chen Ji had gifted her had never existed. Only occasionally would her gaze linger on her empty wrist, where a bracelet Chen Ji had woven through secret techniques once rested—now vanished, along with all the bonds it represented, swept clean by the river of destiny.

In the Demonic Holy Sect, Ye Qing was enduring even more intense anguish. Her memories resembled a book with crucial pages torn away—every fragment involving Chen Ji had become disjointed and vague. She could recall establishing a blood oath with him, yet couldn't remember the oath's substance. She remembered Chen Ji had saved her life, but couldn't pinpoint when or where. This fragmented memory proved more agonizing than complete oblivion, constantly reminding her of something vital she had forever lost. "Chen Ji..." she knelt atop the tower, clutching her head, groaning in torment, "Who are you... Why do I so desperately want to find you..."

Chen Ji observed all this, feeling his heart incrementally tearing apart. Yet his face betrayed no emotion, his gaze colder than ever before. This was the price. The price for shattering destiny. He had believed himself prepared, convinced any sacrifice fell within his calculations. But when genuine loss descended, he finally comprehended—certain things fundamentally resist quantification. Yet he could not regret. Because he knew if he retreated now, he would forfeit far more. Not merely Su Qingyao and Ye Qing, but the third path he had strategically constructed for so long, along with all its unrealized potential.

At this moment, a cold system notification echoed in his mind—the warning mechanism of the Tianji Record: [Third divergent route detected in the River of Destiny. Route stability: 32%. Estimated duration: unknown. Warning: Route stability is positively correlated with host bond completeness. Current bond completeness is insufficient to support long-term route operation. Host is advised to seek new anchor points as soon as possible.] New anchor points? Chen Ji laughed bitterly. He had just personally severed two of the most precious anchor points, and now the Tianji Record was telling him he needed more. This path, as expected, had never offered him any easy options from the very beginning.

choice.prompt: The Tianji Record's notification revealed a harsh truth: the third path requires more anchor points to maintain stability. Who among those around Chen Ji could be a potential candidate?

choices.description: Chen Nian was taken by the Holy Sect to serve as a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key.' Her existence itself can interfere with the Tianji Record's foresight. Rescuing her and establishing a bond might become a completely new stabilizing anchor point—though this means even greater risks.
choices.visible_cost: The Holy Sect's defenses are tightly guarded. A forceful intrusion may expose all hidden cards.
choices.visible_reward: Chen Nian becomes a new anchor point, significantly improving the third path's stability, and may unlock new abilities of the Tianji Record.
choices.risk_hint: Chen Nian's existence will interfere with foresight. You need to personally face unknown dangers.

text.content: Chen Nian. Chen Ji thought of his sister who had been missing for years, remembered his mother's dying request—'Find her, protect her.' She was taken by the Holy Sect and cultivated as a Heavenly Fate Lock Key. This meant she harbored within her some force capable of prying open destiny. If he could rescue her and make her become one of his bonds once more... this might be the hint given by the Tianji Record. He began to mobilize his perception, attempting to lock onto Chen Nian's location. Soon, a vague coordinate surfaced in his consciousness—deep within the Demonic Holy Sect, where lay the answer he had been searching for all along.

choices.description: Ling Yuan is Chen Xuan's predecessor candidate for inheritance, and has long coveted the Tianji Record. Superficially approaching him may allow utilizing an enemy's power as a new anchor point—of course, this could also be making a pact with the devil.
choices.visible_cost: Ling Yuan is profoundly unfathomable. Any vulnerability could be exploited by him.
choices.visible_reward: Through Ling Yuan, penetrate the core of the Tianqing Sect to acquire more resources and intelligence.
choices.risk_hint: Ling Yuan himself is a hidden enemy. This step may invite wolves into the house.

text.content: Ling Yuan. Chen Ji's eyes flickered slightly. This old sect master of the Tianqing Sect had been secretly maneuvering ever since the day Chen Ji obtained the Tianji Record. Superficial protection was in truth reconnaissance and control. But at this moment, Chen Ji conceived another possibility—Ling Yuan's obsession with the Tianji Record could precisely become the focal point he could exploit. Rather than allowing this old fox to watch from the shadows, why not proactively enter the chess game, facing him as a fellow chess player? He did not know whether this was the Tianji Record's hint, or a flash of inspiration after being driven to desperation. But in any case, this was better than sitting idle and waiting for death.

choices.description: Han Lie is the number one genius of the Xuanwu Sect, with overwhelming combat power yet a simple mind. If he could establish some kind of bond with him—even an adversarial one—it could become a new anchor point.
choices.visible_cost: Han Lie's Combat Power far exceeds your current level; the odds of victory in a direct confrontation are extremely low.
choices.visible_reward: After establishing a bond with Han Lie, you can leverage the Xuanwu Sect's resources to greatly enhance your Strength.
choices.risk_hint: Han Lie's hostility runs deep; transforming it into a bond requires an extremely clever scheme.

text.content: Han Lie. Chen Ji remembered that Xuanwu genius he had defeated through stratagem at the Three Great Sects Tournament. After that battle, Han Lie's hatred for him had nearly become tangible—every encounter left Han Lie wishing to tear him to shreds. Yet such extreme emotion conversely signified an extreme bond. Hatred is a connection stronger than indifference. If a way could be found to transform Han Lie's hatred into another form of bond... Chen Ji didn't know if it was possible, but he understood that in his current desperate situation, any possibility was worth attempting.

Just as Chen Ji weighed the pros and cons, the Tianji Record flickered again—this time projecting not a clue, but a blurry vision. In the image, a woman in simple white garments stood within a void, surrounded by the surging River of Destiny. Her features bore a resemblance to Chen Ji's, yet her eyes were clearer than his, like pristine water untouched by worldly matters. This woman raised her head, as if capable of piercing through time and space to meet Chen Ji's gaze. Her lips moved, as if speaking, yet no sound could be conveyed. "Niannian..." Chen Ji's voice trembled slightly. His sister. The last remaining family in this world, and the only variable he refused to calculate when scheming across the realm.

dialogue.content: (Chen Nian stood at the edge of the River of Destiny, surrounded by a faint golden glow—the power of the Heavenly Fate Key was awakening. Her voice pierced through temporal barriers, resonating directly in Chen Ji's mind) "Brother... I know you're watching." Her eyes reddened slightly, yet she struggled to maintain a composed expression. "The Holy Sect people told me I can only gain freedom when you come to find me." She paused, a barely perceptible tremor in her voice, "I'll wait for you. However long it takes."

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at his sister's face in the vision, feeling something deep within him struck with tremendous force. He recalled their mother clutching his hand on her deathbed, entrusting Chen Nian's safety to him; remembered the young Chen Nian hiding behind him, calling out "Brother" in her childish voice; remembered the year Holy Sect cultivators burst into their home, forcibly taking Chen Nian away as she screamed her heart out. These memories should have gradually blurred over the long years, yet this moment of separation reignited them, searing so intensely he could barely breathe. "I'll go." He said quietly, his voice carrying unprecedented resolve, "Once I finish handling things here... I will definitely come to rescue you."

But just then, the Tianji Record's vision suddenly convulsed violently. The Holy Sect guards seemed to have sensed Chen Nian's anomaly—a fierce sword light slashed toward her direction. Chen Nian's figure flickered in the vision, and then—the image vanished. The Tianji Record returned to silence, as if everything just witnessed had been mere illusion. Yet Chen Ji knew it was no illusion. He felt his Heavenly Fate Value drain away once more in that moment—the cost of the Tianji Record attempting to protect Chen Nian, only to be blocked by the Holy Sect's power. "Holy Sect..." A cold light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes, "You'd best pray that before I arrive, you don't harm her in the slightest. Otherwise, I'll let you understand what it truly means to—act the fool before devouring the tiger."

But for now, he had even more pressing matters to attend to. The third path had opened, the price already being extracted, and the two most crucial allies beside him—one had lost all memory of him, while the other struggled painfully within fragmented recollections. Chen Ji drew a deep breath, temporarily suppressing his longing for Chen Nian deep in his heart. What mattered most now was stabilizing the current situation. He closed his eyes, beginning to mobilize the remaining power within the Tianji Record Fragment, advancing with difficulty along that unstable third path. He understood that from this moment forward, he would truly become alone. A solitary chess player bound by no bonds, remembered by no one. Yet this path was his own choice. Since he had chosen it, he could only walk it through to the end.

Just as his consciousness was about to return to his body, Chen Ji saw Su Qingyao turn back in confusion through the crowd—those eyes held not the slightest memory of him. She merely felt an inexplicable heaviness in her heart, as if something precious was slipping away, yet no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't recall what it was. And Chen Ji could only stand in the unseen void, carving this scene into the deepest recesses of his heart, transforming it into the motivation for his continued journey. The price had been paid, the chess game had begun, and he—must win.
